sketches.name: p5-as-source
sketches.description: p5 as a hydra source: p5 draws, hydra transforms.

sketches.name: p5-text-mask
sketches.description: p5 text as a mask over hydra colors, with feedback trails.
sketches.code:
// p5 text as a mask over hydra colors, with feedback trails.
p5 = new P5()
p5.hide()
s0.init({ src: p5.canvas })

p5.draw = () => {
  p5.background(0)
  p5.fill(255)
  p5.textAlign(p5.CENTER, p5.CENTER)
  p5.textStyle(p5.BOLD)
  p5.textSize(p5.height / 4)
  p5.text('HYDRA', p5.width / 2, p5.height / 2 + Math.sin(p5.frameCount / 20) * 60)
}

// the previous frame, slightly zoomed and darkened, under the masked text
src(o0)
  .scale(1.015)
  .hue(0.01)
  .color(0.96, 0.96, 0.96)
  .layer(osc(30, 0.05, 1.4).mask(src(s0)))
  .out()

sketches.name: p5-particles-feedback
sketches.description: p5 particles fed into a hydra feedback loop.
sketches.code:
// p5 particles fed into a hydra feedback loop.
// Uses screen() from hyper-hydra's blend modes, which loads automatically.
p5 = new P5()
p5.hide()
s0.init({ src: p5.canvas })

const dots = Array.from({ length: 120 }, () => ({
  x: p5.random(p5.width),
  y: p5.random(p5.height),
  angle: p5.random(p5.TWO_PI)
}))

p5.draw = () => {
  p5.clear() // transparent, so only the dots reach hydra
  p5.noStroke()
  dots.forEach((d, i) => {
    d.angle += (p5.noise(d.x * 0.002, d.y * 0.002, p5.frameCount * 0.005) - 0.5) * 0.3
    d.x = (d.x + Math.cos(d.angle) * 3 + p5.width) % p5.width
    d.y = (d.y + Math.sin(d.angle) * 3 + p5.height) % p5.height
    p5.fill(255, 150 + 100 * Math.sin(i))
    p5.circle(d.x, d.y, 6)
  })
}

src(o0)
  .scale(0.995)
  .rotate(0.002)
  .hue(0.004)
  .color(0.97, 0.97, 0.97)
  .screen(src(s0).colorama(0.2))
  .out()

sketches.name: p5-webgl
sketches.description: p5 in 3D (WEBGL mode) layered over a hydra trail.
sketches.code:
// p5 in 3D (WEBGL mode) layered over a hydra trail.
p5 = new P5({ mode: 'WEBGL' })
p5.hide()
s0.init({ src: p5.canvas })

p5.draw = () => {
  p5.clear()
  p5.normalMaterial()
  p5.rotateX(p5.frameCount * 0.01)
  p5.rotateY(p5.frameCount * 0.013)
  p5.torus(p5.height / 5, p5.height / 14, 48, 24)
}

src(o0)
  .scale(1.01)
  .rotate(0.003)
  .color(0.95, 0.95, 0.95)
  .layer(src(s0))
  .out()

sketches.name: p5-audio
sketches.description: The microphone drives both p5 and hydra (allow microphone access in the browser).
sketches.code:
// The microphone drives both p5 and hydra (allow microphone access in the browser).
a.setBins(4)

p5 = new P5()
p5.hide()
s0.init({ src: p5.canvas })

p5.draw = () => {
  p5.background(0, 40) // translucent background leaves trails
  p5.noFill()
  p5.stroke(255)
  p5.strokeWeight(6)
  p5.circle(p5.width / 2, p5.height / 2, 100 + a.fft[0] * 600)
  p5.line(0, p5.height / 2, p5.width, p5.height / 2 + (a.fft[3] - 0.5) * 400)
}

src(s0)
  .modulateScale(noise(3, 0.2), () => a.fft[1] * 0.5)
  .kaleid(6)
  .color(1, 0.5, () => 0.3 + a.fft[2])
  .out()

sketches.name: p5-as-controller
sketches.description: p5 as a controller: its mouse and keyboard state drive hydra parameters.
sketches.code:
// p5 as a controller: its mouse and keyboard state drive hydra parameters.
// Nothing is drawn with p5 here; it only reads input.
p5 = new P5()
p5.hide()

shapeSides = 3 // global, so the blocks below can be re-run on their own
p5.keyPressed = () => {
  if (p5.key >= '1' && p5.key <= '9') shapeSides = Number(p5.key) + 2
}

shape(() => shapeSides, 0.3, 0.01)
  .repeat(3, 3)
  .rotate(() => p5.mouseX / p5.width * Math.PI * 2)
  .modulate(noise(2, 0.1), () => p5.mouseY / p5.height * 0.5)
  .color(() => p5.mouseIsPressed ? 1 : 0.2, 0.6, 1)
  .out()

sketches.name: radiolaria-plate
sketches.description: A plate of growing radiolarians after Haeckel, drawn by p5 and softly bloomed by hydra.

sketches.name: radiolaria-specimen
sketches.description: One radiolarian living through its cycles: it grows, sways, dissolves and regrows as a new variation.
sketches.code:
// One radiolarian living through its cycles: it grows, sways, dissolves and regrows as a new variation.
p5 = new P5()
p5.hide()
s0.init({ src: p5.canvas })

r = radiolaria(p5, {
  form: 'bush',
  size: 0.46,
  life: 'cycle', // 'grow' once, 'cycle' forever, or 'still' (fully grown)
  grow: 15,
  cycle: 45,
  arms: 11,
  branching: 3, // levels of side branches
  thorns: 5,
  droop: 0.8, // longer arms hanging down
  symbionts: 60
})

p5.draw = () => {
  radiolaria.backdrop(p5)
  r.draw()
}

// hydra adds a slow watery wobble
src(s0)
  .modulate(noise(1.5, 0.05), 0.008)
  .out()

sketches.name: radiolaria-kaleid
sketches.description: A turning cage on a transparent canvas, folded and trailed by hydra feedback.
sketches.code:
// A turning cage on a transparent canvas, folded and trailed by hydra feedback.
p5 = new P5()
p5.hide()
s0.init({ src: p5.canvas })

cage = radiolaria(p5, {
  form: 'cage',
  life: 'still',
  rings: 4,
  spines: 7,
  branching: 2,
  spin: 0.4,
  // tilt nods back and forth: any option can be a function of time (seconds)
  tilt: (t) => 0.35 + 0.3 * Math.sin(t * 0.3),
  glow: 0.6
})

p5.draw = () => {
  p5.clear() // transparent, so hydra only gets the skeleton
  cage.draw()
}

src(o0)
  .scale(1.008)
  .rotate(0.003)
  .color(0.96, 0.97, 1)
  .layer(src(s0).kaleid(6).luma(0.1))
  .out()

sketches.name: radiolaria-evolve
sketches.description: Evolving forms: options given as functions of time make the skeleton change shape as it lives.
sketches.code:
// Evolving forms: options given as functions of time make the skeleton change shape as it lives.
p5 = new P5()
p5.hide()
s0.init({ src: p5.canvas })

swing = (t, period, lo, hi) => lo + (hi - lo) * (0.5 + 0.5 * Math.sin(t * 2 * Math.PI / period))

left = radiolaria(p5, {
  form: 'ring',
  x: 0.28,
  size: 0.3,
  life: 'still',
  rings: (t) => Math.round(swing(t, 40, 1, 4)), // rings are added and taken away
  spines: (t) => Math.round(swing(t, 25, 8, 20)),
  spineLength: (t) => swing(t, 13, 0.6, 1.4),
  curl: (t) => swing(t, 17, -0.4, 1.2)
})

right = radiolaria(p5, {
  form: 'star',
  x: 0.72,
  size: 0.3,
  life: 'still',
  blades: (t) => Math.round(swing(t, 30, 10, 26)),
  bladeWidth: (t) => swing(t, 11, 0.5, 1.6),
  teeth: (t) => Math.round(swing(t, 19, 0, 8)),
  palette: 'gilded'
})

p5.draw = () => {
  radiolaria.backdrop(p5, { palette: 'gilded' })
  left.draw()
  right.draw()
}

src(s0).out()

sketches.name: radiolaria-audio
sketches.description: Audio-reactive lattice: the bass pushes the spines out, the mids make it swell and the highs make it glow.
sketches.code:
// Audio-reactive lattice: the bass pushes the spines out, the mids make it swell and the highs make it glow.
// The browser asks for microphone access the first time.
p5 = new P5()
p5.hide()
s0.init({ src: p5.canvas })

a.setBins(4)
a.setSmooth(0.85)

sphere = radiolaria(p5, {
  form: 'lattice',
  life: 'still',
  spines: 40,
  spineLength: () => 0.3 + a.fft[0] * 1.5,
  size: () => 0.36 + a.fft[1] * 0.08,
  glow: () => 0.5 + a.fft[2] * 2,
  spin: 0.25,
  palette: 'neon'
})

p5.draw = () => {
  radiolaria.backdrop(p5, { palette: 'neon', grain: 0.4 })
  sphere.draw()
}

src(s0)
  .blend(src(o0).scale(1.02), 0.5)
  .out()

extensions.name: hydra-arithmetics
extensions.author: geikha
extensions.description: Visual arithmetics: mod, step, pow, min, max, trigonometry, ranges and coordinate sources.

extensions.name: hydra-arrays
extensions.author: geikha
extensions.description: Operate between arrays and generate new ones: add, mult, wrap, shuffle, Array.run, Array.random...

extensions.name: hydra-blend
extensions.author: geikha
extensions.description: Blending modes from raster image software (screen, overlay, softLight...). Also redefines layer, mask and luma for better alpha handling.

extensions.name: hydra-canvas
extensions.author: geikha
extensions.description: Control hydra's canvas: size, alignment and pixel interpolation.

extensions.name: hydra-colorspaces
extensions.author: geikha
extensions.description: Work with color in other colorspaces: CMYK, HSV, HSL, YUV, YIQ.

extensions.name: hydra-convolutions
extensions.author: geikha
extensions.description: Convolution kernels as sources: blur, sharpen, sobel, prewitt, edge... or define your own.

extensions.name: hydra-debug
extensions.author: geikha
extensions.description: Adds .debug() to read and live-edit the fragment shader of a sketch.

extensions.name: hydra-fractals
extensions.author: geikha
extensions.description: Mirroring and inversion functions that make fractals when fed back.

extensions.name: hydra-gif
extensions.author: geikha
extensions.description: Load animated .gif files into a source with s0.initGif(url).

extensions.name: hydra-glsl
extensions.author: geikha
extensions.description: Write GLSL code directly in your patches.

extensions.name: hydra-gradientmap
extensions.author: geikha
extensions.description: Create gradients from css colors and use them for gradient mapping.

extensions.name: hydra-mouse
extensions.author: geikha
extensions.description: Replaces the mouse object, adding normalized and canvas-relative positions (mouse.posx, mouse.cposy...).

extensions.name: hydra-outputs
extensions.author: geikha
extensions.description: Change the framebuffer settings of outputs: linear interpolation, wrapping, buffer count.

extensions.name: hydra-pip
extensions.author: geikha
extensions.description: Toggle picture-in-picture for the hydra canvas with hydraPip().

extensions.name: hydra-pixels
extensions.author: geikha
extensions.description: Read pixel values from hydra's outputs with o0.read(x, y).

extensions.name: hydra-src
extensions.author: geikha
extensions.description: srcAbs and srcRel show sources at their original size or aspect ratio.

extensions.name: hydra-swizzle
extensions.author: geikha
extensions.description: GLSL-style swizzling: osc().gbr, gradient().r, noise().xxyw...

extensions.name: hydra-tap
extensions.author: geikha
extensions.description: Tap tempo and beat envelopes (beats, beats_). Ctrl+Space+Shift pauses, Ctrl+Shift+number sets speed.

extensions.name: hydra-text
extensions.author: geikha
extensions.description: Text as a hydra source: text(), strokeText(), fillStrokeText().

extensions.name: hydra-vec4
extensions.author: geikha
extensions.description: Construct colors like GLSL's vec4(), vec3() and vec2().

extensions.name: hydra-wrap
extensions.author: geikha
extensions.description: Change how textures wrap (mirror, repeat, clamp) with hydraWrap. Redefines src, scroll and related functions.

extensions.name: hydra-abbreviations
extensions.author: geikha
extensions.description: Write very small hydra code: o(), ns(), sh(), .bl(), .df()... Add it with + to use it.

extensions.name: Color manipulation
extensions.author: Thomas Jourdan
extensions.description: Color filters: sepia, levels, monotone, gradients, hsvshift and vector-math color mixing.
examples:
osc(4, 0.1, 1.2)
  .levels(4, 0.8)
  .out(o0)
gradient(1).hsvshift(() => time % 1, 1, 1).out(o1)
noise(3).monotone(3, 0.6, 1).out(o2)
voronoi(5).grarose(1).out(o3)
render()

extensions.name: if then else
extensions.author: Thomas Jourdan
extensions.description: Switch between two sources depending on a value: ifpos, ifzero, ifeven, splitview.

extensions.name: Noise generators
extensions.author: Thomas Jourdan
extensions.description: Noise and turbulence sources inspired by F. Kenton Musgrave: turb, warp, cwarp, ncontour...
examples:
turb(3, () => time * 0.1, 5).out(o0)
warp(3, () => time * 0.1, 4, 4, 2).out(o1)
ncontour(0.5, 0.05, 4, 2, 0.1, 4).out(o2)
colornoise(2, 1).out(o3)
render()

extensions.name: Soft patterns
extensions.author: Thomas Jourdan
extensions.description: Patterns with smooth transitions, similar to osc() but with more complex shapes: blobs, blinking, smoothsun...

extensions.name: Op-art patterns
extensions.author: Thomas Jourdan
extensions.description: Op-art patterns: spiral, brick, checker, hextile, lissa, pulse...

extensions.name: Screen space operations
extensions.author: Thomas Jourdan
extensions.description: Post-processing in screen space: dithering, blur, edge detection, erode/dilate, pixel sort.

extensions.name: Space transforms
extensions.author: Thomas Jourdan
extensions.description: Coordinate transforms: invtile, invsqrt, abslog, swave, centermag.

extensions.name: Periodic waves
extensions.author: Thomas Jourdan
extensions.description: Basic periodic sources: square, triangle, sawtooth and harmonic waves, straight or radial.

extensions.name: moebius
extensions.author: hesserrepi
extensions.description: A twisting Möbius band knotted into a trefoil, engraved with fine lines, with oval eyes cut through it. engrave() hatches any source the same way.

extensions.name: lissajous
extensions.author: hesserrepi
extensions.description: Lissajous figures as oscilloscope traces: one figure with any frequencies, or the whole table of ratios and phase shifts.

extensions.name: chladni
extensions.author: hesserrepi
extensions.description: The nodal lines of a vibrating square plate, as on Chladni's sound figures: one plate that morphs between grids, crosses and rings, or a table of engraved plates.

extensions.name: hydra-ink
extensions.author: hesserrepi
extensions.description: Click and drag to push the colours around like ink on water. Modes: push (smear), fluid (stirred fluid) and comb (marbling, hold still to drop ink).

extensions.name: radiolaria
extensions.author: hesserrepi
extensions.description: Growing radiolarian skeletons after Haeckel's Stephoidea plate, drawn with p5: spiny rings, lattice spheres, cages, thorny arms, symbionts around a red capsule. Six forms, every option can change over time.
examples:
p5 = new P5()
p5.hide()
s0.init({ src: p5.canvas })
radiolaria.plate(p5)
src(s0).out()

p5 = new P5()
p5.hide()
s0.init({ src: p5.canvas })
r = radiolaria(p5, { form: 'bush', life: 'cycle', size: 0.45 })
p5.draw = () => { radiolaria.backdrop(p5); r.draw() }
src(s0).modulate(noise(2, 0.1), 0.01).out()
